description:
Join our NASA Space Apps Challenge team! We're building an AI-powered decision-support tool that uses NASA Earth observation data—soil moisture, crop health, and climate—to help farmers choose crops and plan rotation.

We need teammates with skills in:

Programming & software development

AI & machine learning

Data analysis & visualization

UI/UX and app design

Agriculture or environmental science

Diverse skills make better solutions—come build with us!

details:
OMNIFARM is an intelligent agricultural system that integrates satellite data from NASA, meteorological information, and data from soil sensors to assist farmers in land management. The system offers six core functions: identifying bare land, assessing climate adaptability, selecting suitable crops, managing irrigation systems, estimating root distribution, and measuring crop density.

By monitoring soil moisture, temperature, rainfall, and crop growth, the system enables farmers to make data-driven decisions, .We developed a product that provides farmers with agricultural solutions, allowing them to monitor crop information like soil density and rootstock positions in real time to improve farming efficiency. By doing annual inspections and maintenance, we tackle issues like parts aging and damage. Plus, by combining real-time data monitoring with NASA data and AI analysis, we can overcome program errors like data monitoring mistakes. This product can further boost productivity, reduce manual work, cut labor costs, save time, and improve farm management efficiency. It uses NASA satellite data and AI to monitor soil, crops, and moisture, helping farmers make smarter decisions and increase yields.

such as determining which crops to plant, when to irrigate, and precisely calculating the amount of water required for irrigation.

Our project helps conserve water, promote crop growth, reduce resource waste, and enhance a farm's resilience to climate change. Its innovation lies in the integration of above-ground crop monitoring and below-ground root analysis into a single, unified system.

To achieve this, we utilized NASA data, employed Python and JavaScript programming languages, and incorporated soil moisture sensors, meteorological sensors, and irrigation systems. Throughout the development process, we took a comprehensive range of factors into account, including soil conditions, climatic variables, crop types, root depth, crop density, water consumption, and agricultural production costs.
